report.source_text: On physical examination at the current presentation, the patient’s muscle strength in her lower extremities was as follows: right: 3/5 and left: 1/5 (proximal/distal, respectively). There was a sensory level in the thoracic region (T6), and spastic hyperreflexia was present in the lower extremities (American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) impairment scale C). Urinary sphincter function was intact, but the patient complained of incomplete evacuation of the bladder. A urodynamic study revealed a spastic bladder. Bilateral Babinski reflexes were upward.

report.source_text: Emergency whole-spine contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 that was hyperintense in T2-weighted images (Figure 1a), with scattered enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1b). Additionally, there was a round intradural extramedullary mass lesion at the L1 and L2 levels causing a compression effect on the conus medullaris that was isointense in T2-wighted images (Figure 1c), with homogenous enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1d).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman with a history of Ewing sarcoma of the left clavicle (diagnosed December 2019, treated with surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy) achieved complete metabolic response on PET scan in March 2021. In August 2021, approximately 5 months after documented remission, she presented with progressive paraparesis and paresthesia over 1 week, manifesting as right lower extremity weakness 3/5, left 1/5, sensory level at T6, spastic hyperreflexia, bilateral upward Babinski reflexes, and spastic bladder with incomplete evacuation (ASIA impairment scale C). Emergency spinal MRI revealed two distinct metastatic lesions: (1) a large intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 with T2 hyperintensity and scattered contrast enhancement, and (2) an intradural extramedullary mass at L1-L2 with isointense T2 signal, homogenous enhancement, and compression of the conus medullaris. Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion confirmed Ewing sarcoma, demonstrating small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, true rosette formations in a pauci-vascular background, diffuse strong CD99 immunoreactivity, high Ki-67 proliferative index (85–90%), and negative LCA staining. Postoperative imaging following surgical decompression showed appropriate decompression of the thoracic lesion and complete resolution of the lumbosacral lesion. At 10-month follow-up (approximately June 2022), the patient's neurological status had deteriorated further, with bilateral lower extremity strength declining to 0/5 (ASIA impairment scale B), persistent spasticity, and urofecal retention. The patient remained alive with disease at the time of the 10-month follow-up report.

final.final_diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma with metastatic spinal involvement (intramedullary thoracic and intradural extramedullary lesions)
final.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman with a history of Ewing sarcoma of the left clavicle (diagnosed December 2019, treated with surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy) achieved complete metabolic response on PET scan in March 2021. In August 2021, approximately 5 months after documented remission, she presented with progressive paraparesis and paresthesia over 1 week, manifesting as right lower extremity weakness 3/5, left 1/5, sensory level at T6, spastic hyperreflexia, bilateral upward Babinski reflexes, and spastic bladder with incomplete evacuation (ASIA impairment scale C). Emergency spinal MRI revealed two distinct metastatic lesions: (1) a large intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 with T2 hyperintensity and scattered contrast enhancement, and (2) an intradural extramedullary mass at L1-L2 with isointense T2 signal, homogenous enhancement, and compression of the conus medullaris. Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion confirmed Ewing sarcoma, demonstrating small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, true rosette formations in a pauci-vascular background, diffuse strong CD99 immunoreactivity, high Ki-67 proliferative index (85–90%), and negative LCA staining. Postoperative imaging following surgical decompression showed appropriate decompression of the thoracic lesion and complete resolution of the lumbosacral lesion. At 10-month follow-up (approximately June 2022), the patient's neurological status had deteriorated further, with bilateral lower extremity strength declining to 0/5 (ASIA impairment scale B), persistent spasticity, and urofecal retention. The patient remained alive with disease at the time of the 10-month follow-up report.
